coherence.reasons: Both run a consistent launch / sizing / packaging / trade-off pyramid to the same recommendation. X's slide 3 ties five must-be-true conditions to verdicts, and those verdicts map directly onto the revised answer, the later sections and the five decisions requested. Its flaw is the 'only option' claim in the governing thought and slide 9 title: its own table shows the add-on also clears the margin floor and reaches +4.3 NRR points at the top of its range, which X concedes ('Pro and the add-on overlap'). Y's four-part structure is tighter, but its 'prize' section sizes the add-on it rejects while the governing thought plans on Pro's $2.9M. Y also calls 26% uptake the gate while planning on the 33% point estimate, and its $2.4M net figure includes a win-back ceiling it has just discounted. X's hierarchy holds together slightly better.

judgment.reasons: Both land on the answer key's preferred recommendation: Pro tier with a usage allowance, sized off the paywall test, mobile delay accepted explicitly. X weighs more alternatives with numbers: free-in-Core (breaks the margin floor), add-on, Pro without allowance, and mobile-first. On mobile-first it admits the ARR comparison is a close call that may slightly favour mobile, and names the 2028 NRR timing as the deciding factor. It also shows the regressive effect of a flat fee on small accounts (+63% at 3 seats) against price being 22% of churn, and sets breakpoints (26%, 21%), a pre-launch non-volunteer test with go/no-go thresholds and a fallback rule. Y weighs the mobile delay by netting it at its ceiling and sets sensible conditions, but never evaluates mobile-first or a free bundle as options. Y also plans on the 33% high case as a point estimate and starts the non-volunteer test only in Q2, at launch. X's recommendation is better defended.

evidence.reasons: Both get the required calculations right: $8.06M vs $2.45M, inference at $32 / $61 / $130, 109 wins and $0.64M, Pro at $2.89M, and company margin scenarios (both reach 74.1% uncapped). Both reject the Sales memo and flag volunteer and survey bias. X goes further: it discounts the 14% for beta skew (flagged as an assumption), computes add-on gross profit after platform cost, gives ranges rather than point estimates, shows a half-attribution case for the win-rate drop, and notes new-logo ARR does not count toward NRR. It also catches two inconsistencies in the pack (58% vs a computed 40% usage share; 1,190 vs 1,372 churned accounts). X's weak points are the arbitrary seat-ratio scaling to 10.7%, the thin 3.8 vs 4.0 point argument that retention alone cannot reach the target, and the 'only option' overclaim. Y adds two good observations: loss notes cover all lost deals, and recovering a third would beat the pre-AI win rate. But its $2.4M net figure adds a ceiling-case Pro uptake and a ceiling win-back that it has itself discounted, labels both as 'risks at their ceiling', and leaves out inference cost. Its capped margin of 75.7% is also thin against the floor and not stress-tested.

revision.reasons: Both revise the CPO's hypothesis the way the key expects: keep the launch, reject the $149 add-on and the $8M sizing, replace with paywall-based figures. X does this explicitly, breaking the hypothesis into five conditions and showing which fail (46% demand, flat-fee economics), which hold (customer value, need to launch) and which hold only conditionally (mobile delay). It then maps the failures to the packaging change and resets the plan to a $1.7–2.9M range. Y's revision is correct and clear ('size on what accounts paid, not what admins said'), but less systematic, and it replaces $8M with a single $2.9M figure resting on the 2023 tier precedent at its upper bound.

overall.reasons: The two documents reach the same defensible recommendation with correct core numbers, and Y is admirably concise. X would serve the executive team better for four reasons: it gives ranges and breakpoints rather than a high-case point estimate; it compares Copilot-first with mobile-first candidly; it evaluates the free-bundle alternative against the margin floor; and it sets a pre-launch non-volunteer test with go/no-go gates and concrete decisions. It also surfaces inconsistencies in the pack's data. Its 'only option' framing is overclaimed, but the body of the document discloses the overlap with the add-on.
